title: Add RAG dependency-graph workbench and session-playback CLI for debugging tool-call flows
author: Marisol Vega
release_notes: New developer workbench: dependency-graph visualizer and a session-playback CLI to reproduce and assert RAG execution flows locally; docs page and quickstart added; non-breaking example tooling improvements.
ci_checks: e2e-smoke: pass (rerun after flaky playback test)
description: Motivation: Debugging complex RAG tool-call topologies and KV-cache interactions is time consuming; engineers frequently need to reproduce a failing session end-to-end, visualize tool dependencies, and assert intermediate tool outputs. This PR introduces two complementary developer-facing tools: 1) a dependency-graph workbench (web-based static demo + local electrum-style bundle) that renders tool-call DAGs, cache hit/miss annotations, and per-node timing/profile overlays; 2) a session-playback CLI that can ingest recorded traces (redwood .rtrace format) and replay requests against local stubs or live endpoints with deterministic seeding, producing trace diffs and step assertions. The change also adds three new RAG example templates (parallel-fanout-agent, sequential-kv-proxy-agent, and conditional-router-agent) and a docs quickstart page under Developer Workbench. Summary of commits: commit 1: scaffold dependency-graph renderer and sample corpus (workbench/web + static JSON serializer); commit 2: implement session-playback CLI (play, diff, assert subcommands), deterministic seeding and stub adapters; commit 3: add example templates and typesafe tool-binding stubs (TS + Python); commit 4: docs, templates, and CI smoke tests for playback. Changed areas (high-level): - workbench/web/: new static demo and renderer (D3-based minimal graph layout) and sample corpora; - tools/playback/: Rust-based CLI entrypoint with a thin TS shim for local stubs; - examples/templates/: three RAG templates (parallel-fanout, sequential-kv-proxy, conditional-router); - docs/devworkbench.md: new quickstart and debugging walkthrough; - tests/ci/playback-smoke/: e2e smoke harness and assertions; - telemetry/probes/: small probe to export trace fragments to .rtrace. Testing notes: added unit tests for deterministic seeding, CI includes an e2e smoke job that runs the playback CLI against local stubs. One playback test was flaky on first CI run due to a race in stub startup; fixed with a 200ms backoff retry and re-ran. Review thread highlights: Kai: "Nice ergonomic tooling — two asks: document the rtrace schema and add a small JSON schema for quick validation; also can we ensure playback exits non-zero on assertion failure?"; Marisol: "Added rtrace-schema.json in telemetry/probes and updated CLI to return non-zero on assert failures; expanded docs to show example error codes."; Elena: "Renderer is great, but layout needs stable node ids for animation between runs — suggest using deterministic hashing of tool name + invocation index."; Marisol: "Switched layout to use MurmurHash-based ids; added tests to ensure stability across equivalent traces."; Dante: "CI flake fixed; approve after cleanup of a stray console.log."; Marisol: "Removed leftover console.log and squashed commits for merge." CI and merge: initial CI run showed one flaky playback-smoke test (playback-stub-liveness) which failed; rerun passed. Post-merge actions: create follow-up ENG task to add a VSCode devtool for rendering inline graphs (ENG-3029) and a perf baseline for graph render latency. Docs site update: docs/devworkbench.md added with step-by-step quickstart, example traces, and a short troubleshooting table. UX note: the workbench is intentionally shipped as a read-only static bundle in this PR (no backend) to avoid onboarding friction; a future PR will add live websocket annotations for dedicated/private deployments. Merge outcome: merged to main via squash, changelog entry added in docs/changelog.md.
